result.summary: The pedestrian environment is situated under a large highway overpass, which creates significant shadows and visual obstructions from massive support pillars. While a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks are present, the lack of signalization and the wide, multi-lane roadway increase risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Large concrete pillars of the overpass obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the crossing point.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the crosswalk

hazards.name: Poor Lighting
hazards.description: The area under the overpass is significantly darker than the surrounding street, reducing the visibility of pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire roadway under the overpass

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Wide Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without the protection of a signal or a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to provide a safe waiting area and allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Enhanced Crosswalk Lighting
interventions.description: Install dedicated, high-visibility lighting for the crosswalk to counteract the shadows cast by the overpass.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The environment is dominated by heavy transportation infrastructure, including a highway overpass and tram tracks embedded in the roadway. While a sidewalk and bike lane are present on one side, the overall scale and lack of pedestrian-oriented features like street trees or a continuous sidewalk network create a relatively hostile environment.

hazards.name: Embedded Rail Tracks
hazards.description: Tram or trolley tracks in the roadway can catch bicycle tires and create tripping hazards for pedestrians crossing the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending into the distance

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The right side of the roadway lacks a sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to cross or walk in the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the retaining wall

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway without a median refuge increases pedestrian exposure to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway crossing

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to break up the crossing distance and provide a safe waiting area.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a sidewalk on the right side of the street to provide a continuous and safe path for pedestrians on both sides.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility (continental or ladder style) crosswalk across the main thoroughfare to clearly define pedestrian space.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment includes a marked zebra crosswalk, curb ramps, and dedicated bike lanes, providing basic accessibility. However, the presence of embedded trolley tracks and a high perimeter wall introduces tripping hazards and limits visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Embedded Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks embedded in the roadway surface can be slippery and pose a tripping hazard for pedestrians or catch bicycle tires.
hazards.location_in_image: Running across the foreground and middle ground of the roadway.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: The high concrete wall on the left side of the image restricts visibility for both pedestrians entering the crosswalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Large wall on the left side of the street.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Signage
interventions.description: Add pedestrian crossing signs or RRFBs to better alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is situated under a large highway overpass, featuring wide, well-maintained sidewalks with tactile paving and a dedicated green bike lane. While basic infrastructure like pedestrian signals and curb ramps are present, the massive bridge columns create significant visual obstructions and a desolate atmosphere.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Bridge Columns
hazards.description: Large concrete support columns for the overpass block sightlines between turning vehicles and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and background, supporting the overhead structure.

hazards.name: Desolate Environment
hazards.description: The area under the overpass lacks active land use or 'eyes on the street', which can decrease perceived safety and security.
hazards.location_in_image: Area directly under the bridge structure.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space and increase visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Enhanced Under-Bridge Lighting
interventions.description: Install bright, pedestrian-scale lighting under the overpass to eliminate dark spots and improve visibility at all hours.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight past the columns.
